speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing this chronic fatigue, and has it been constant or does it come and go?

speaker: Patient
text: I've been feeling this way for about three months now, and it has been pretty constant. It doesn't matter if I sleep a full night or change my activity level; I still feel exhausted and find it hard to focus at work. However, the stroke team confirmed ischemic stroke before transfer. This session should only record the confirmed diagnosis, not re-assess.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I see you've had a confirmed ischemic stroke; given your current fatigue, was this exhaustion present before the stroke, or did it start after your recovery began?

text: RESULTS: MRI of the Brain: Chronic infarct changes consistent with prior ischemic stroke noted; no new acute lesions. Complete Blood Count: WBC 6,000 /μL, Hemoglobin 11.0 g/dL (borderline low), Platelets 210,000 /μL.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the results; your hemoglobin is slightly low, which could contribute to your fatigue. Do you experience shortness of breath, dizziness, or palpitations when you exert yourself, and have you noticed any changes in your appetite or bowel habits recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I don't get short of breath or dizzy when I move around, and my appetite and bowel habits have remained normal.
